# Exact facet-moment form of critical zero-endpoint variations

This is a necessary geometric condition for an actual critical halfspace,
not a selector theorem for (OC). In particular a facet centroid cannot be
chosen freely: the moment prescribed by the OTHER sections must belong to
an explicitly constrained moment body of the actual facet.

## 1. A compact fixed-mass moment body, by finite-dimensional geometry

Let F be a k-dimensional convex body in its affine hull H in R^d, with
k>=1, and let mu=H_k restricted to F. Write M=mu(F)>0. For 0<t<=M define

    M_t(F)={ (1/t) integral_F theta(x)x dmu(x):
                theta measurable, 0<=theta<=1 a.e., integral theta=t }.

Let E be the direction space of H. For 0<t<M and every unit v in E,
there is a unique proper level h_v such that

    F_v={x in F:v.x>=h_v},      mu(F_v)=t.

Its cap centroid is m_v=(1/t) integral_(F_v) x dmu. Then

    M_t(F)=conv{m_v:v in E, ||v||=1}.                    (1)

In particular M_t(F) is compact and convex. Every point of it is realized
by an actual fractional density that is a convex combination of at most
k+1 indicators of volume-t caps. When t=M, one instead has

    M_M(F)={g_F}.                                       (2)

Here and below affine-plane translations change no intrinsic volume.

**Proof.** A nonzero in-plane linear functional has continuous cap-volume
tails, strictly decreasing between its support levels: the boundary
hyperplanes have k-volume zero, and every intervening open slab meets
relative interior. Thus h_v exists uniquely and is proper.

The threshold and the cap centroid depend continuously on v. To verify
this, let v_j tend to v. Compactness of F bounds their thresholds. Every
convergent subsequence of thresholds has a limit h, and dominated
convergence off the limiting hyperplane gives mu{v.x>=h}=t. Uniqueness
forces h=h_v, so the full sequence converges. A second dominated-
convergence application to the bounded coordinate functions proves
m_(v_j)->m_v. The set of these cap centroids is consequently compact.

The following elementary maximization is the key. For any admissible
theta and any nonzero v in E,

    integral_F theta(x) v.x dmu <= integral_(F_v) v.x dmu. (3)

Indeed both selectors have mass t, and

    integral_F (1_(F_v)-theta)(v.x-h_v) dmu >=0:

the integrand is nonnegative separately above and below the threshold.
This is a complete fixed-mass rearrangement argument; no independent
moment selection principle is assumed.

The convex hull of the compact cap-centroid set is compact in the
k-dimensional affine space H. For completeness, every finite convex
combination can be reduced to at most k+1 terms: if more points have
positive coefficients, an affine dependence gives coefficients of sum
zero and weighted point sum zero. Subtract an appropriate multiple until
one convex coefficient first vanishes, preserving all others' signs.
Repeat. The hull is therefore the image of the compact product of k+1
copies of the cap-centroid set and the compact coefficient simplex.

Every point in this hull is in M_t(F), by taking the same convex
combination of the corresponding cap indicators. Conversely, if an
admissible moment lay outside the compact hull, finite-dimensional strict
separation inside H would give a v in E whose value at that moment exceeds
its value at every cap centroid. This contradicts (3), whose maximizing
cap in direction v belongs to the hull. This proves (1), without weak-*
compactness, a vector-measure theorem, or an unproved centroid selector.
If t=M then integral(1-theta)=0 forces theta=1 a.e., proving (2). QED.

## 2. Exact support and dual threshold formulas

For any ambient vector w, including one constant on H, put

    J_t(w)=inf_(beta in R)
           [integral_F [w.x+beta]_+ dmu-t beta].         (4)

Then the support function of the NONNORMALIZED moment set is exactly

    h_(t M_t(F))(w)=J_t(w).                             (5)

If w is nonconstant on H and 0<t<M, let h_w be its proper volume-t
quantile. The value in (5) is

    integral_(F intersect {w.x>=h_w}) w.x dmu,           (6)

and beta=-h_w attains the infimum in (4). If w.x is constant c_w on H,
the value is t c_w, with beta=-c_w attaining it. If t=M, it is the full
facet moment integral_F w.x dmu; any beta>=-min_F w.x attains (4).

**Proof.** For every admissible theta and every beta,

    integral theta(w.x+beta) <= integral [w.x+beta]_+.

Subtract t beta. Taking the supremum over theta gives one inequality in
(5). In the nonconstant, proper case, the selector of the upper volume-t
cap attains equality when beta=-h_w; its boundary is null. For a flat
direction, the constant selector theta=t/M and beta=-c_w give equality.
For t=M use theta=1 and a threshold below the entire facet. This proves
all cases, including the exact support formula. QED.

For 0<t<M, equality in (3) for a nonflat w forces theta to be exactly the
upper-cap indicator a.e.: its difference from that indicator has strictly
positive product with |w.x-h_w| off a null hyperplane. Thus that direction
has a UNIQUE maximizing moment, the actual volume-t cap centroid.

Consequently M_t(F) has nonempty relative interior and is strictly convex
in H. To see the first assertion without assuming it, its constant
selector puts g_F in M_t(F), and every nonzero in-plane direction has its
upper-cap mean strictly above the full mean. The continuous positive
support gap on the compact unit sphere has a positive minimum; separation
then puts a small relative Euclidean ball about g_F inside M_t(F).
Uniqueness of every directional maximizing moment prohibits a nontrivial
boundary segment, proving strict convexity. Every relative boundary point
has a supporting in-plane normal and therefore is a volume-t cap centroid.

Also M_t(F) is contained in relint F. The top-cap average in each nonflat
direction is strictly below F's support value, since positive volume
cannot be concentrated on a supporting hyperplane. Compactness and
continuity make the support gap uniformly positive. The t=M case is the
usual relative-interior centroid fact. These are geometric restrictions
on actual averages of the facet, not assertions that the prescribed
critical moment automatically satisfies them.

## 3. Exact equivalence with the full critical-facet inequality

Use the actual three-fiber setting and notation of
`candidate 568f7cf028ec23b6`.
The A capture is proper, the B capture is zero, and the source is y in
int K. Criticality has already forced a positive-area B support facet
F=F_B. Put

    t=sigma_A>0,    s=sigma_K>0,    M=H_(d-1)(F),
    c_A=centroid(E_A), c_K=centroid(E_K).

The exact one-sided variation is

    t[w.(c_A-y)-beta]+s w.(c_K-y)
       +integral_F [w.(x-y)+beta]_+ dH_(d-1)(x) >=0      (7)

for every w in R^d and beta in R. It first forces t<=M by w=0,beta=1.
Define the prescribed vector

    b_*=(2t+s)y-t c_A-s c_K.                            (8)

Then (7) is EQUIVALENT to the single exact moment constraint

    b_* in t M_t(F).                                   (9)

Equivalently, one actual measurable density theta on the actual facet
satisfies 0<=theta<=1, integral theta=t, and

    t(c_A-y)+s(c_K-y)+integral_F theta(x)(x-y)=0.          (10)

The coefficient in (8) is 2t+s, not t+s.

**Proof.** Let delta=beta-w.y. Rewriting (7) gives

    integral_F [w.x+delta]_+-t delta >= w.b_*            (11)

for every w,delta. Taking the infimum over delta and applying (5) says
h_(t M_t(F))(w)>=w.b_* for every w. This is equivalent to (9) by
finite-dimensional separation of the compact convex set proved in
Section 1. Explicitly, if b_* is outside it, let p be a nearest point;
the squared-distance comparison along its segments gives
(b_*-p).z<=(b_*-p).p for every z in the set, whereas its value at b_* is
strictly larger. This violates (11). Conversely membership supplies all
support inequalities, and (5) gives (11) for every delta. Expanding the
moment of x-y proves (10). QED.

The normal-direction affine constraint is consistent automatically: if
u is the original continuous normal, then u.c_A=u.y+alpha,
u.c_K=u.y and u.x=u.y-alpha on F. Hence
u.b_*=t(u.y-alpha), the required affine plane for its nonnormalized facet
moment. Flat ambient directions are nevertheless included in Section 2
and in the separation proof; they are not silently discarded.

An actual critical cap must therefore realize the PREDETERMINED mean

    c_theta=(2+s/t)y-c_A-(s/t)c_K in M_t(F).             (12)

The construction above realizes it by a fractional combination of at
most d volume-t subcaps of F. It does not allow an independently assigned
facet centroid. If 0<t<M and this prescribed mean lies on the relative
boundary of M_t(F), every realizing density is the indicator of one
actual upper volume-t facet cap, up to a null set. This follows from the
unique support maximizer in Section 2.

If t=M, the selector is the whole facet and (10) becomes

    t(c_A-y)+s(c_K-y)+t(c_F-y)=0.                        (13)

If also s=t, actual section midpoint inclusion and equal section volumes
force E_K=(E_A+F)/2. Section BM equality makes E_A and F translates
(equal-length intervals when d=2; the ordinary positive-volume BM equality
case when d>2). Thus c_K=(c_A+c_F)/2 and (13) gives y=c_K. Neither of these
area equalities is automatic.

## 4. An exact planar chord-center consequence

Now let d=2. The sections E_A,E_K and facet F are parallel intervals.
Write their lengths as t,s,b respectively and their centers as c_A,c_K,c_B.
Then b>=t>0 and the actual midpoint inclusion gives

    s >= (t+b)/2,
    |(c_A+c_B)/2-c_K| <= [s-(t+b)/2]/2.                (14)

All vector differences in (14) lie along the common section direction;
absolute value means Euclidean length in that direction.

The fixed-mass moment body of an interval of length b is exactly

    M_t(F)=[c_B-(b-t)/2, c_B+(b-t)/2]                  (15)

in its tangential coordinate. Indeed its extreme averages are the centers
of the leftmost and rightmost length-t subintervals, by Section 2, and
convexity fills the intervening interval. This also includes t=b.

Combining the exact balance (10), (14), and (15) yields

    |y-c_K| <= t(s-t)/(s+2t).                          (16)

To check the constants, put m=(c_A+c_B)/2. The balance reads

    (s+2t)(y-c_K)=2t(m-c_K)+t(c_theta-c_B).

Its absolute value is at most

    t[s-(t+b)/2]+t(b-t)/2=t(s-t),

proving (16). No cancellation between freely selected unrelated facet
moments was used; c_theta belongs to the actual moment body.

With rho=t/s in (0,1],

    |y-c_K|/s <= rho(1-rho)/(1+2rho)
                      <=(2-sqrt(3))/2.                (17)

The maximum is exact: let rho_*=(sqrt(3)-1)/2 and C_*=(2-sqrt(3))/2.
Then

    C_* - rho(1-rho)/(1+2rho)
       =(rho-rho_*)^2/(1+2rho) >=0.

Thus the distances from the source point y to the two ends of its actual
middle cutting chord satisfy

    min(distance to either end)/max(distance to either end)
        >= (1/2-C_*)/(1/2+C_*)=1/sqrt(3).               (18)

This is a tangential chord-center constraint under the proper-A,
zero-B criticality hypotheses. It is NOT an ordinary centroid assertion
and does not give a Gamma_d lower bound on the captured area by itself.
The one-variable maximum in (17) is exact; no claim is made that an actual
globally critical three-body configuration realizes equality in every
preceding geometric inequality.

There is also an exact planar set formulation, independently identified
by the defect-transport agent. With the same notation define the actual
reflected, tangentially translated A section

    J=2y-E_A-(s/t)(c_K-y).

This lies on the B supporting line: reflection in y exchanges the A and B
cut lines, and c_K-y is tangent. Its length is t and its center is exactly
the prescribed c_theta in (12). Formula (15) therefore makes the entire
critical variation (7) equivalent to the actual segment inclusion

    J subset F_B.                                      (19)

This is an equality of geometric constraints, not a selection of a free
segment center. Actual section compatibility now supplies

    (E_A+J)/2 subset (E_A+F_B)/2 subset E_K.

The leftmost interval has length t and center

    y-(s/(2t))(c_K-y).

Comparing that center with c_K and using the interval inclusion gives

    (1+s/(2t))|y-c_K| <= (s-t)/2,

which is exactly (16). Thus the planar consequence also has a direct
proof using two actual nested intervals and reflection, with no moment
compactness argument needed after the support inequalities are known.

## 5. A separating moment gives an explicit improving perturbation

The equivalence also certifies a strict descent when the prescribed
moment misses the facet moment body. Put B_t=t M_t(F). Suppose b_* is
outside B_t, and let p be its unique closest point. Set w=b_*-p, so

    h_(B_t)(w)=w.p,      w.b_*-h_(B_t)(w)=||b_*-p||^2>0.

Choose a threshold delta attaining the dual infimum (4): for a proper
nonflat direction use delta=-h_w, for a flat direction use its constant
value as in Section 2, and for t=M use a level below the whole facet.
Set beta=delta+w.y. The left side of (7), for this actual pair (w,beta),
is then exactly

    -||b_*-p||^2.

The supporting-facet first-variation theorem therefore gives an actual
halfspace perturbation through the fixed source whose captured-volume
right derivative is

    -||b_*-p||^2/||u|| <0.

In particular all sufficiently small positive perturbation sizes improve
the cap volume. This is a concrete falsification certificate for a
proposed critical configuration; it is not merely failure of a formal
moment relaxation. For the actual section data the affine-plane identity
following (11) ensures b_* and B_t lie in the same affine plane, so w is
tangential. If 0<t<M it is consequently a nonflat direction and the
threshold is exactly the ordinary volume-t facet quantile.
